Fixed. verify_responder_is_delegated_by now takes the caller verifier instead of hardcoding DefaultVerifier.

The bead was right, and the rustdoc was worse than silent about it: it justified the hardcoding as "The signature verifier is DefaultVerifier, matching the rest of verify_ocsp_responder". That is exactly backwards. Line 1416 passes the caller verifier to verify_chain; line 1486 hardcoded DefaultVerifier. The comment asserted the opposite of the code one line below it.

Impact, worse direction first: a verifier STRICTER than DefaultVerifier (refusing an algorithm by policy) had that policy silently bypassed on the single check standing between the caller and a DN-twin responder -- the precise attack the binding exists to stop, per the rustdoc above it. Other direction: a verifier supporting an algorithm DefaultVerifier does not would see a valid responder rejected with OcspDelegation even though the same key verified the whole chain a line earlier.

Private fn, one call site, so no public API change.

Test: the_delegation_binding_honours_the_callers_verifier in pkix-chain/tests/verify_ocsp_responder.rs. The verifier permits the first signature (so verify_chain succeeds) and refuses the next -- a verifier refusing everything would fail inside verify_chain and prove nothing about which verifier the binding used. Same fixture as verify_ocsp_responder_ok, so the verifier is the only variable.

Verified by mutation: restoring the hardcoded DefaultVerifier makes the test fail by returning Ok(ValidatedPath{..}) where the caller had refused. Note two sites in lib.rs match the naive pattern (1499 in this fn, 1862 in signed_by); 1499 is the one.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2345 tests.
